asp_wolf_nights.accept_text: Thin the pack on Blackneedle Rise, east of camp, where the lodgepole starts. Not all of them. I will not have it said that we came into somebody else's country and emptied it. The bears are a separate matter. One has been at the smokehouse and has stopped being frightened of people, and that is the point at which it stops being a bear and starts being a problem.

asp_uphill_boar.accept_text: The highrunners come up off the Slide, west of this meadow, and work its edges at first light. They are fast and they are desperate, and those are two different problems arriving at the same time. Drop the frostspeakers first. Three years they have been trying to pray the cold back down, and whatever it is they are actually doing, it is the thing keeping the rest of them on their feet.

asp_cornered_cold.accept_text:
They are pressed into the deep end where the ice still holds, and they come out as far as the standing water to feed. Go in by the shaft and work inward. It gets colder and it gets older and they get worse the further you go. If you meet the big one before you are ready for him, come back out. He will still be there. He has nowhere else.

The Weeping Ice is the cave on the east side of the rim, north-east of camp. Hesta keeps watch at its mouth.

asp_what_came_across.accept_text: I have put the hide, the hair and the apothecary's own letter into one bundle with my mark burned into the wrap. Rimehowl's hide comes first - he is at the bottom of the Weeping Ice, north-east of camp. Then take the bundle north, down off the mountain, to Tull at Camp Taurajo. Three years ago that man asked whether there was still a road south. The honest answer is that there is no road, there is a mountain, and the mountain has things living in it that are not from here and never were. He will want to be sitting down for the second part.

asp_winch_house.accept_text: The ledgers are in the iron chest under the drum. If the damp has left me three. The mail is loose in the sorting rack and some of it will have blown into the scrub by now - bring whatever is still readable. I know roughly what is in most of it. I would still rather hold it than keep guessing.

asp_wrong_side.accept_text: I will not dress it up for you. They are suffering, they are going to keep suffering, and the only thing anyone can do for them is the thing nobody volunteers for. Them. Do it clean and do it from the front, because they will not run and it is worse if you make them try to.

asp_rope_trade.accept_text: Windcallers first. The plain ones mob you, but it is the callers that turn a mob into a problem, and I would prefer you came back, because you are a repeat customer and those are precious. Coils sees me through the season. I pay fair, which in my family is treated as a confession.

asp_green_wood.accept_text: Standing dead, not fallen. Fallen has been lying in the wet and it is no use to me whatever it looks like on the outside. Bolts will tell me whether the rot runs up from the root or down from the crown. Watch the lynx while you are cutting - they lie up in the deadfall and you will be bent over with an axe and your back to the slope.

asp_first_planks.accept_text: Boards. Not six attempts - I would put in a wall. The whole thing is the first cut. Get that off true and every board after it is off true, and you will not find out until the wall is up and the door will not close. Take your time on the first one. The rest follow it whether you want them to or not.

asp_winter_meat.accept_text: Aspen elk. Work the edges of the stands, not the middle. They cross between cover in the same places every day, and up here that is the only predictable thing about them. Good haunches. Leave the thin ones - we are not so short that we take a poor animal, and I would rather not find out what we become once we start.
asp_winter_meat.turn_in_text: All of them, and not a thin one among them. You hunted the edges. I will be good at this in another two winters. I would rather have stayed bad at it on open ground, but nobody asked me and nobody is going to.

asp_cable_run.accept_text: Follow it down to the face and look at where it enters. The harpies have been at the loose ends - they want the wire for their nests and they have taken what they could reach. Bring me pieces and I can tell you how it parted. Mind the rim. It is a long way down and there are only a few places to do it on purpose.
